designDecisionsAndRationale: The retained TaskDispatcher evaluates reachable topology once, reserves atomically, and carries full-provenance placement into the existing workflow runner and authenticated worker path (§17.2/§17.4).
The exact reserved root consumes the task launch token; called workflows use ordinary process admission and frozen admitted definitions (§17.2).
Authored workspace takes precedence over optional controller default; unresolved remote workspace fails before reservation (§17.4).
Retained uncertain-launch fencing prevents local or alternate-worker fallback after a claim (§17.2).
intentionalTradeoffs: Keep tightly coupled SHD-1–SHD-5 in one serial plan with one code/test owner (§17.7).
Retain earlier positive V1/V11 host logs only as checkpoint evidence; rerun affected gates on final source.
A bounded V5 baseline exception may permit slice review while V5 remains failing and parent P1 remains open.
supportedEdgeCases: Explicit worker/group pins, stale capabilities, zero capacity, absent live worker, dependency wait and pre-reservation version races.
Called-workflow reachability, reused node IDs across steps and callees, instance patches, missing targets and workspace aliases.
Worker loss after claim, uncertain launch, no duplicate attempt/job, durable terminal reconciliation and old controller JSON decoding.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Task-level live cancellation acknowledgment, director child accounting, task-backed examples and legacy removal.
Credential-backed model equivalence, new service APIs, schema migration and final parent certification.
